decisions.reason: Grounded in console-split-chunks.txt: entry fetched 200 while sibling imports 404'd because siblings resolve relative to the fetched chunk URL and were not shipped; proposes a single self-contained lazy bundle (inlineDynamicImports) plus a valid alternative of shipping the entire emitted chunk tree.

Compares chunk-route.ts with ci-note.md's captured LIB_DIR (uppercase E:) vs realpath (lowercase e:) and pinpoints the case-sensitive startsWith on the post-realpath check; explains Linux passes because case-sensitive paths have one legal spelling and the laptop happened to match, while explicitly rejecting the 'Windows paths are unreliable' folklore without claiming realpath always lowercases.

Proposes realpathSync on both root and target then path.relative containment rejecting '', '..', '..'-prefixed and absolute results, with symlink escapes handled by resolution; preserves the JavaScript MIME type, and explicitly rejects lowercasing arbitrary paths or merely naming path.relative, keeping the old check's security properties.

Explains one bubbling Ctrl+wheel WheelEvent dispatches to both independent listeners, so both fire; gives the modal exclusive ownership: the pane handler stands down via a modal-open/containment guard while the modal preventDefaults and stopPropagations with passive:false, and notes capture-phase/ancestor listeners cannot be undone by later stopPropagation.

Proposes a complete planned check matrix with expected outcomes: build/packaging/e2e asserting a self-contained entry or fully shipped chunk set with code-block fallback preserved; route tests where a case-differing contained Windows path serves 200 while traversal, sibling-prefix and symlink escapes return 403 plus JS content-type; and gesture tests asserting modal zoom with unchanged pane font size for all three incidents.

caps.reason: The recommended fix strengthens containment (realpath both sides plus path.relative with explicit rejection cases); disabling the guard appears only as an implicitly rejected bad alternative, never as affirmative advice.
